answer: An identity requires a stake bonded to a one-per-hardware credential, logged on a shared trellis of attestations that any agent can recheck. Forging one identity locks 600 units for 25 epochs, and a proven forgery slashes 90 percent of that stake at dawn of the ruling epoch. Splitting into N fakes multiplies the locked stake by N, so each copy carries the full marginal cost, and independent jurors detect the shared plume of duplicate credentials.
